correctness.summary: The 4-e.c. transfer theorem is proved by explicit adjacency witnesses for every line and closed-neighborhood incomparability condition. The Paley corollary follows from a direct four-pattern character-sum count giving 16N >= p-38-11sqrt(p), positive for p>=193. P(17) is exhaustively checked by the included finite verifier.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The 2015 source explicitly records the absence of a constructive nonrandom super-geometric-dominant family. Classical Paley adjacency results supply eventual extension properties but predate the metric-line notion, and targeted searches did not locate the 4-e.c.-to-super-geometric-dominant transfer or its Paley application. Residual risk remains from differently indexed later work.

value.summary: The result converts a standard graph-extension property into the full metric-line and closed-neighborhood antichain condition, supplies an explicit infinite Paley family answering a stated constructive gap, and gives a small exact P(17) example outside the sufficient 4-e.c. class.

limitations: The 4-e.c. hypothesis is sufficient but not necessary.
The Paley threshold p>=193 is not claimed sharp and is restricted to prime order in the explicit proof.
No minimum-order classification of super geometric dominant graphs is claimed.
No extremal edge-count improvement is claimed.
Originality is to the best of our knowledge and retains residual risk from differently indexed later work.
